standard_prerequisites.name: The standing equivalence between Koszul-regular, H1-regular and quasi-regular for the theory used here, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited at proof lines 5755-5756 as used without further mention
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the three regularity notions be handled in the same framework.

standard_prerequisites.name: Permanence of regular immersions and regularity of the composite of a regular immersion with a regular immersion, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited at proof lines 5802-5804 and again at 5826-5828
standard_prerequisites.use: Closes the first case and lets a closed immersion into an affine space be adjoined without losing regularity.

standard_prerequisites.name: A closed immersion of a smooth scheme into a smooth scheme over the same base is a regular immersion
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the regular immersion into an affine space used to reduce the H1-regular case.

standard_prerequisites.name: Factorization of a smooth morphism through an étale morphism to an affine space over the base, together with the formal étale lifting identities for graded pieces of ideals
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the quasi-regular case to the affine space case and to the étale case, where the associated graded pieces of the two ideals are identified.

core_obligations: Reduce to the case where the target is an affine space over an affine base with the second immersion closed: after shrinking, write the base and the source as spectra of rings, realize the first immersion by a surjection of a polynomial ring, choose lifts of the images of the variables, and exhibit the ideal of that closed immersion as the sum of the ideal generated by the differences of the variables with their lifts and the extended ideal of the base ideal (proof lines 5757-5775).

Prove the affine space case: show that the displayed three-term sequence of conormal modules is split exact by noting that the ideal generated by the differences is free with those differences as a basis and that the Kaehler derivative maps those generators to the basis of the module of differentials, and conclude from the factorization through the regular immersion cut out by a regular sequence together with the cited permanence lemma and the splitting of the associated conormal sequence (proof lines 5776-5805).

H1-regular case: after shrinking to affine schemes choose a closed immersion of the smooth total space into an affine space over the base, which is regular by the cited statement, so the composite of the given H1-regular immersion with it is again H1-regular by the composition statement, reducing to the previous case; the author notes that this step does not work in the quasi-regular case (proof lines 5807-5830).

Quasi-regular case: factor the smooth morphism through an étale morphism to an affine space over the base by the cited factorization, so it remains to handle the affine space case, already proved, and the case where the smooth morphism is étale (proof lines 5832-5838).

Etale case: shrink to affine schemes with both immersions closed and the ideal of the first immersion generated by a quasi-regular sequence; since the ring map is étale it is formally étale, so the graded pieces of the ideals of the two closed immersions are isomorphic, whence the base ideal is generated by a quasi-regular sequence as well (proof lines 5840-5846).
proof_roadmap: Handle the case of an affine space over an affine base by exhibiting the ideal of the immersion and splitting its conormal sequence (proof lines 5757-5805).

Reduce the H1-regular case to it by embedding the smooth total space regularly into an affine space, and the quasi-regular case by factoring the smooth morphism through an étale map and comparing graded pieces for an étale base change (proof lines 5807-5846).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that in a commutative triangle with a smooth morphism X to S and two immersions, if the immersion of Y into X is Koszul-regular, respectively H1-regular or quasi-regular, then so is the immersion of Y into S (statement lines 5740-5753). The counted proof is long and organized by cases: it computes the ideal of the immersion explicitly in the case of an affine space over an affine base and proves that the associated conormal sequence splits, which reduces that case to a cited permanence statement; it then handles the H1-regular case by embedding the smooth total space regularly into an affine space, and the quasi-regular case by factoring the smooth morphism through an étale map to an affine space and identifying the graded pieces of the two ideals through formal étaleness (proof lines 5755-5846). It is H2: the case analysis and the reductions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the standard permanence, regularity and factorization statements.
